title: CHAPTER 1: ESSENCE OF PSYCHOLOGY
content:
ሰላምታዬ ከያላችሁበት ይድረሳችሁ ውድ የEthioFresh ቤተሰቦች! 💖👋 አዲስ የዩኒቨርሲቲ ሕይወት እንዴት ይዟችኋል? ዛሬ ደግሞ የFreshman ኮርስ የሆነውን General Psychology (Psyc 1011) Chapter 1 Part 1 Tutorial ይዘንላችሁ መጥተናል። ይህ ኮርስ ስለ ሰው ልጅ ባህሪ እና አእምሮ የሚያጠና በመሆኑ ለህይወታችንም እጅግ ጠቃሚ ነው። በፈተና ላይ (በተለይ Case Questions) 100% ውጤት እንድታመጡ በሚያስችል መልኩ ሞጁሉን መስረት አድርገን፣ በቂ ዝርዝር መረጃዎችን አካተን፣ በእንግሊዝኛም በአማርኛም እያንዳንዱን ነጥብ ዘርዝረን አዘጋጅተንላችኋል። በፈገግታ በአብሮነት ወደፊት 🏄ቅ🏄🏻‍♂️👇👇👇 !

1.1. Definition of Psychology and Related Concepts

• Etymological Definition (የቃሉ አመጣጥ): The word ‘psychology’ is derived from two Greek words: ‘psyche’ (mind, soul, or spirit) and ‘logos’ (study, knowledge, or discourse). Therefore, epistemologically, psychology means the study of the mind, soul, or spirit. It is often represented by the Greek letter Ψ (psi).
• Scientific Definition: Psychology is formally defined as the scientific study of human behavior and the underlying mental processes.
• This definition highlights three core aspects that must be understood thoroughly:
1. Science: Psychology relies on scientific methods, systematic observation, experimentation, and empirical data gathering rather than commonsense, intuition, or personal beliefs.
2. Behavior: Refers to any observable and measurable action or reaction of an organism. Behavior includes both overt activities (outwardly visible actions such as talking, walking, facial expressions, and body movements) and covert responses (internal physiological responses like heartbeat changes or muscle tension).
3. Mental Processes: Refers to all the internal, hidden activities of our minds that cannot be directly observed by others. These include cognitive processes such as thinking, reasoning, remembering, feeling, perceiving, and dreaming.

👉
የሳይኮሎጂ ትርጉም (Definition): ሳይኮሎጂ የሚለው ቃል የመጣው ከሁለት የግሪክ ቃላት ሲሆን፣ እነሱም ‘Psyche’ (አእምሮ፣ ነፍስ ወይም መንፈስ) እና ‘Logos’ (ጥናት ወይም እውቀት) ናቸው። በመሆኑም በቃሉ አመጣጥ ደረጃ የነፍስ ወይም የአእምሮ ጥናት ተብሎ ይተረጎማል። በአሁኑ የሳይንስ ትርጉሙ ግን ሳይኮሎጂ ማለት የሰዎችን ባህሪ (Behavior) እና አእምሯዊ ሂደቶችን (Mental processes) በሳይንሳዊ መንገድ የሚያጠና ትምህርት ነው።
ባህሪ (Behavior) ስንል በግልጽ የሚታዩ (Overt - እንደ መናገር፣ መሳቅ) እና የማይታዩ (Covert - እንደ የልብ ምት መጨመር) ድርጊቶችን ያጠቃልላል። አእምሯዊ ሂደቶች (Mental processes) ደግሞ በውስጣችን የሚከናወኑ እንደ ማሰብ፣ ማስታወስ እና ስሜት ያሉ ናቸው። ሳይኮሎጂ ሳይንስ የሆነበት ምክንያት በሙከራና በመረጃ (Empirical data) ላይ ስለሚመስረት እንጂ በግምት ወይም በልማዳዊ አስተሳሰብ (Commonsense) ስለማይመራ ነው።


1.2. Goals of Psychology

As a formal science, psychology strives to achieve four primary goals in understanding human behavior and mental processes:

1. Description (What is happening?): This goal involves observing behavior and noting everything about it as objectively and detailed as possible. It addresses questions such as: What is happening? Where does it occur? To whom does it happen? And under what circumstances?
• Module Detailed Case Example: A teacher notices that a freshman university girl is behaving oddly in class—she fails to turn in her homework, displays a negative attitude toward learning, and frequently distracts her peers during lectures.
2. Explanation (Why is it happening?): Explanation goes beyond mere observation to understand the causes behind the observed behavior. It attempts to find reasons and form tentative theories to explain why a particular behavior occurs.
• Module Detailed Case Example: Upon investigating, the teacher discovers that the student behaves this way because she receives extra attention (reward) from her peers whenever she acts out, reinforcing her disruptive behavior.
3. Prediction (What will happen in the future?): Based on understanding past and present observations, prediction aims to determine how humans will think or act in the future under specific conditions.
• Module Detailed Case Example: The teacher predicts that if this pattern of behavior and peer reinforcement continues unchecked, the student will never reach her full academic potential and may eventually fail her university courses.
4. Control (How can it be changed?): Control involves altering, modifying, or managing conditions to transform undesirable behavior into desirable, adaptive behavior.
• Module Detailed Case Example: The teacher implements specific educational and behavioral modification strategies—such as rewarding her only when she submits assignments and encouraging focused study habits—to help her succeed academically.

👉
የሳይኮሎጂ አላማዎች (Goals):
1. Description (መግለጽ/ማስተዋል): “ምን እየተፈጠረ ነው?” ብሎ የሰዎችን ባህሪ ሳይደብቁ በጥንቃቄ መመዝገብና መመልከት።
2. Explanation (ማብራራት): “ለምን ተፈጠረ?” ብሎ የባህሪውን መንስኤና ምክንያት መፈለግ።
3. Prediction (መተንበይ): “ወደፊት ምን ሊፈጠር ይችላል?” ብሎ አሁን ባለው ሁኔታ ላይ ተመስርቶ የቀጣዩን ውጤት መገመት።
4. Control (መቆጣጠር/መቀየር): የማይፈለግ መጥፎ ባህሪን ወደ ጥሩ (ወይም ከውድቀት ወደ ስኬት) “እንዴት መቀየር ይቻላል?” ብሎ መፍትሄና ስትራቴጂ መስጠት።

💡 Exam Hint & Case Question Tip: ፈተና ላይ በሚመጡ የCase ጥያቄዎች ላይ፡ ግለሰቡ ምን እያደረገ እንደሆነ ብቻ ከተገለጸ መልሱ Description ነው። ለምን ያንን ድርጊት እንደፈፀመ ምክንያቱ ከተገለጸ Explanation ነው። ወደፊት ሊከሰት የሚችል ውጤት ከተገመተ Prediction ነው። መፍትሄ ወይም የባህሪ ማስተካከያ ዘዴ (Therapy/Strategy) ከተሰጠ ደግሞ Control ይሆናል!


1.3. Historical Background and Early Schools of Psychology

• Psychology as an independent scientific field is relatively young (around 125+ years old). Before the late 19th century, questions about the mind were handled primarily by philosophy and physiology.
• Formal scientific psychology began in 1879 in Leipzig, Germany, when Wilhelm Wundt established the first psychological laboratory. Because of this historic contribution, Wundt is recognized as the “father of modern psychology”. He utilized a self-observation technique known as objective introspection to examine basic mental processes.

1.3.1. Early Schools of Psychology
A ‘school of thought’ refers to a systematic view and theoretical approach shared by a group of psychologists regarding the nature of the mind and behavior. The five major early schools include:

1. Structuralism:
• Founder: Edward Titchener (a student of Wilhelm Wundt).
• Focus: Investigating the fundamental structure of the human mind.
• Goal: To break down conscious experience into its basic units or elements (such as sensations, feelings, and images).
• Method: Introspection (“looking inward into one’s own conscious experience”).
2. Functionalism:
• Founder: William James (the first prominent American psychologist).
• Focus: Studying the functions of the mind and behavior rather than its structure.
• Core Belief: Examined how mental processes enable organisms to adapt, survive, work, and flourish in their environment.
• Method: Used objective observations, questionnaires, and psychological tests.
3. Gestalt Psychology:
• Founder: Max Wertheimer (and colleagues in Germany, early 20th century).
• Focus: Studying the mind and perception as a whole. The German word “gestalt” translates to form, configuration, or organized pattern.
• Core Belief: Summarized by the famous statement: “The whole is greater than the sum of its parts.” They argued that breaking down consciousness into elements destroys its essential meaning.
4. Behaviorism:
• Founder: John B. Watson.
• Focus: Studying strictly observable and measurable behaviors while completely rejecting unobservable mental processes.
• Core Belief: All human behavior is learned through interaction with the environment (nurture over nature). Learners are seen as passive entities responding to environmental stimuli.
5. Psychoanalysis:
• Founder: Sigmund Freud (an Austrian physician from Vienna).
• Focus: Studying the unconscious mind and early childhood experiences.
• Core Belief: Unconscious drives, sexual/aggressive urges, and unresolved early childhood traumas drive human behavior and may express themselves as physical symptoms called ‘hysteria’. Freud likened the mind to an iceberg, where the conscious mind is merely the visible tip.
• Method: Clinical case studies using free association, hypnosis, and dream analysis.

• Key Differences among Early Schools: Early schools of psychology differed across three fundamental aspects: their Object of study (what aspect of mind or behavior they examined), their Goal (what outcome they sought), and their Method (how they gathered their data).

👉
የቀደምት የሳይኮሎጂ አስተሳሰቦች (Early Schools of Thought):
1. Structuralism: አእምሮ ከምን ከምን እንደተሰራ (Structure) ማለትም ህሊናችንን ወደ ትንሹ ክፍሎች (ስሜት፣ ምስልና ፍላጎት) በመክፈል በራስ ምርመራ (Introspection) ያጠናል።
2. Functionalism: አእምሯችን አካባቢን ተላምደን እንድንኖር፣ እንድንሰራና እንድንተርፍ (Adapt and survive) እንዴት እንደሚያገለግል (Function) ያጠናል።
3. Gestalt: አእምሮን ከፋፍለን ሳይሆን በአጠቃላይ (As a whole) ማጥናት አለብን ይላሉ። ምክንያቱም "አጠቃላይ ስብስብ ከክፍሎቹ ድምር ይበልጣል" ብለው ስለሚያምኑ ነው።
4. Behaviorism: አእምሮ ውስጥ ያለውን በዓይን ማየት ስለማንችል፣ በግልፅ የሚታየውንና የሚለካውን ባህሪያችንን ብቻ (Observable behavior) ማጥናት አለብን ይላሉ። ባህሪ በዘር ሳይሆን ከአካባቢ የሚማር ነው ብለው ያምናሉ።
5. Psychoanalysis: ፍሮይድ (Freud) እንዳለው ደግሞ አብዛኛው ባህሪያችን የሚመነጨው ከማናውቀው (Unconscious) የአእምሮ ክፍላችን እና በልጅነታችን ከደረሰብን የሥነ-ልቦና ጠባሳ ነው። ህልም መፍታት (Dream analysis) እና ነፃ ንግግርን (Free association) ይጠቀማል።

💡 Exam Hint:
• Wundt = Father of modern psychology (1879, Leipzig Laboratory).
• Structuralism = Introspection & Elements of mind (Titchener).
• Functionalism = Adaptation & Survival (William James).
• Gestalt = Whole pattern (Max Wertheimer).
• Behaviorism = Observable behavior & Environmental learning (John B. Watson).
• Psychoanalysis = Unconscious mind, childhood trauma, & Iceberg analogy (Sigmund Freud).

😂 የሳይኮሎጂ ቀልድ: አንድ የBehaviorism አራማጅ እና የPsychoanalysis አራማጅ ተገናኝተው ወሬ ጀመሩ። የPsychoanalysis አራማጁ (Freud) ጓደኛውን፣ "ዛሬ ያዘንከው እኮ በልጅነትህ አባትህ ከረሜላ ስለከለከለህ ነው" አለው። የBehaviorism አራማጁ (Watson) ደግሞ መለሰ፣ "አይደለም! ያዘንኩት በልጅነቴ ሳይሆን አሁን አንተ አጠገቤ ቆመህ ስለሚያስጠላኝ (Environment) ነው!" ተባባሉ ይባላል። 😂 (ሁለቱም የየራሳቸውን School of thought እያስረገጡ ነው!)
